    Blind Rescue Horse Quickly Declining Gets Medical Care He Needs to Survive

    October 20, 2026 Andrea Powell
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:33
    Instaread

    A blind senior horse named Airforce was taken in by Gentle Spirit Horses in need of medical care and a safe place to call home.

    The gelding is estimated to be in his twenties and has struggled to maintain his weight and health. Tests revealed he has Cushing's disease, which will require medication and special care to manage. He lost his vision due to complications from leptospirosis.

    Photo: Gentle Spirit Horses Rescue

    Another recent decline in healing from minor wounds and keeping weight on Airforce, common issues in horses with Cushing's disease, had caretakers worried. 

    The rescue shared with us, "Despite supportive care, his condition continued to raise concern, and euthanasia was being considered due to his overall lack of improvement."

    Thanks to your donations, he is getting the vital daily medication Prascend, which was a key component in stabilizing his condition.

    Photo: Gentle Spirit Horses Rescue

    "Alongside dental work and adjustments to his feeding program, the medication helped regulate his underlying hormonal imbalance. As a result, Airforce began to regain weight and show measurable improvement in his overall condition. In addition to physical improvements, we also observed a noticeable reduction in his anxiety. As a blind horse, stress management is an important part of his quality of life, and improved metabolic stability appears to have contributed to a calmer, more settled demeanor." 

    Photo: Gentle Spirit Horses Rescue

    He is now happily grazing alongside his horse friends who help him navigate the pasture. Thank you for giving him a second chance to thrive in his golden years. Your donations are changing lives. 

    Please consider donating to help more rescued horses in need. 
    Andrea Powell

    Andrea Powell is an animal enthusiast who resides in West Michigan. When not writing, she is exploring the great outdoors with her dogs and horses.
